# Sampletable

# Number of chimeric fragments

```{r cnts, results='asis', cache=TRUE}
cnts <- list()

for (sp in spt[['samplename']]) {
  prfx <- paste0('../data/rnaseq_rilseq/', sp, '/', sp)
  # total and mapped reads
  cnts[[sp]] <- total_mapped(paste0(prfx, '_R1.cutadapt.fastq_bwa.bam.rillibsize'))
  # all rilseq fragments
  cnts[[sp]][['all_fragments']] <- fragments(paste0(prfx, '_all_fragments.txt'), 'total')
  # single rilseq fragments
  cnts[[sp]][['single_fragments']] <- fragments(paste0(prfx, '_all_fragments.txt'), 'single')
  # chimera rilseq fragments
  cnts[[sp]][['chimera_fragments']] <- fragments(paste0(prfx, '_all_fragments.txt'), 'chimera')
 # significant rilseq fragments
  cnts[[sp]][['significant_fragments']] <- fragments(paste0(prfx, '_significant_fragments.txt'), 'total')
}
```

```{r, results='asis'}
cnts.df <- data.frame(t(
    do.call(cbind, cnts)))
# there was header lines, so remove 1
cnts.df[['all_fragments']] <- lapply(cnts.df[['all_fragments']], function(x) {x-1})
cnts.df[['significant_fragments']] <- lapply(cnts.df[['significant_fragments']], function(x) {x-1})
cnts.df[['ratio_signif_all_fragments']] <- lapply(rownames(cnts.df), function(x) {
    cnts.df[x, 'significant_fragments'][[1]] / cnts.df[x, 'all_fragments'][[1]]})
cnts.df[['ratio_signif_mappedreads']] <- lapply(rownames(cnts.df), function(x) {
    cnts.df[x, 'significant_fragments'][[1]] / cnts.df[x, 'mapped'][[1]]})

cols <- c('ratio_signif_all_fragments', 'ratio_signif_mappedreads',
          'significant_fragments', 'all_fragments',
          'single_fragments', 'chimera_fragments',
          'mapped', 'total')
knitr::kable(cnts.df[cols])
```

# Summary plots

## Single vs. chimeric

```{r, results='asis'}
sub.df <- cnts.df %>%
  select(single_fragments, chimera_fragments) %>%
  mutate(sample = rownames(cnts.df)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(! sample, names_to='fragment_type', values_to='raw_count')
sub.df[['raw_count']] <- unlist(sub.df[['raw_count']])

ggplot(sub.df, mapping = aes(x=sample, y=raw_count, fill=fragment_type)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust=1))
```


# Summary_RILSeq_S-chimeras

```{r, results='asis'}
cat(paste0('\n\n**Link to output file:** [Summary_RILSeq_S-chimeras_',
           subgroup_i, '.xlsx](Summary_RILSeq_S-chimeras_', subgroup_i, '.xlsx).'))
```

The RILseq output files `{sample}_all_fragments.txt`, containing all single and chimera fragments, and
`{sample}_significant_fragments.txt`, containing significant interactions chimera fragments, are used to
generate the `Summary_RILSeq_S-chimeras.xlsx` file.

The updated annotation [`r params$gtf`](`r params$gtf`)
was used to map the start coordinate
of the significant chimeric fragments RNA1 and RNA2. The annotation contains mRNAs, 5' UTRs, 3' UTRs, sRNAs,
antisense and intergenic regions. RNA1 and RNA2 of each significant chimera are assigned a feature when their
supporting fragments start coordinate overlap with the feature. All features are reported in case of
overlapping features. When the supporting fragments overlap with several features, they are all reported,
unless the percentage of RNA reads overlapping with a gene is more than the min_ratio (0.7), in that case
only the feature with the majority of reads is reported.

The summary excel table contains a subset of the columns from the significant chimera files, and additional
gene information from the annotation. Individual sample tabs contain the following columns:

- `ID`: sample name
- `RNA1.EcoCyc.ID`; `RNA2.EcoCyc.ID`: gene ID from Ecocyc associated with RNA1 and RNA2 respectively of the significant chimera
- `TypeRNA1`; `TypeRNA2`: feature type associated with RNA1 and RNA2 respectively
- `RNA1_name`; `RNA2_name`: gene name
- `RNA1_description`; `RNA2_description`: gene description / function
- `Start.of.RNA1.first.read`; `Start.of.RNA2.first.read`: start coordinate of first RNA read supporting the chimera
- `Start.of.RNA1.last.read`; `Start.of.RNA2.last.read`: start coordinate of last RNA read supporting the chimera
- `RNA1.strand`; `RNA2.strand`: strand of RNA read
- `interactions`: number of interaction supporting the chimera RNA1-RNA2
- `other.interactions.of.RNA1`: number of interaction of RNA1 other than with RNA2
- `other.interactions.of.RNA2`: : number of interaction of RNA2 other than with RNA1
- `total.other.interactions`: total other interactions
- `odds.ratio` and `Fisher.s.exact.test.p.value`: described in https://github.com/asafpr/RILseq.

Additonal tabs are aggregating the biological replicates. Only chimera regions with identical RNA1 and RNA2
associated features are included in those tabs. They summarize interactions found in both replicates.


The following paragraph is copied from https://github.com/asafpr/RILseq and explains the calculation
for significant chimera:

> Reporting Over-represented Interacting Region
>
> Since the sequencing results contain non-specific chimeras, another stage is needed to remove the noise
> of the experiment. This is done by comparing the number of reads supporting an interaction to the number of
> reads expected at random. Simply put we compute a 2x2 contingency table with the number of reads like this:
>
|               | region 1      | other regions |
|---------------|:-------------:|--------------:|
| region 2      |  K            |         L     |
| other regions |  M            |         N     |

> L and M include the number of single reads as well, the statistics test if two regions interact more
> frequently than expected by random. If K is larger than expected the two regions are probably in actual
> interaction in vivo. The odds ratio is computed by (K/L)/(M/N) and the p-value is computed using Fisher's
> exact test, testing only if K is larger than expected (single-tailed test)
>
> The interacting regions are searched by dividing the genome to 100 nt non-overlapping windows (set with
> --seglen) and testing if the number of interactions is larger than expected if there are at least 5
> interactions between them (set with --min_int). If the p-value is smaller than 0.05 (--max_pv) report this
> pair. To avoid re-reporting adjacent regions, the regions can be expanded up to 500 nts (--maxsegs) and the
> combination of regions with the lower p-value will be reported (after Bonferroni correction).


```{r read_chimeras_input, results='asis', cache=TRUE}
#*  Add gene names for RNA1 and RNA2 and count number of libraries for
#*  each chimera. Currently, the unified s-chimeras are generated from
#*  two samples only.
#

# import annotation
gtf_file <- params$gtf
cat(paste0('\n\nAnnotation file is ', gtf_file, '.\n\n'))
annotation <- import(gtf_file, format="GFF")

get_fn <- function(sample.i, group) {
  return(paste0('../data/rnaseq_rilseq/', sample.i, '/', sample.i, '_', group, '_fragments.txt'))
  }

sig.chimeras <- list()
fragments <- list()

for (sample.i in spt[['samplename']]){
  # read significant chimeras (from _significant_fragments.txt)
  sig.chimeras[[sample.i]] <- read.csv(get_fn(sample.i, 'significant'), sep='\t')
  # read all chimeras (from _all_fragments.txt)
  fragments[[sample.i]] <- read.csv(get_fn(sample.i, 'all'), sep='\t', header=FALSE)
  names(fragments[[sample.i]]) <- c('RNA1.chromosome', 'Start.of.RNA1.first.read', 'RNA1.strand',
                      'RNA2.chromosome', 'Start.of.RNA2.first.read', 'RNA2.strand',
                      'name', 'type')
}

# unified samples significant fragments
unified <- list()
for (gp in unique(spt[['group']])) {
  unified[[gp]] <- read.csv(get_fn(paste0(gp, '_unified'), 'significant'), sep='\t')
}
```


```{r get_RNAnames, results='asis', cache=TRUE, dependson='read_chimeras_input'}
RNA1_cols <- c(
  'RNA1.chromosome',
  'Start.of.RNA1.first.read',
  'Start.of.RNA1.last.read',
  'RNA1.strand')
RNA2_cols <- c(
  'RNA2.chromosome',
  'Start.of.RNA2.last.read',
  'Start.of.RNA2.first.read',
  'RNA2.strand')

# the fragment df does not have Start.of.RNA#.aste.read:
RNA1_cols_fg <- c(
  'RNA1.chromosome',
  'Start.of.RNA1.first.read',
  'Start.of.RNA1.first.read',
  'RNA1.strand')
RNA2_cols_fg <- c(
  'RNA2.chromosome',
  'Start.of.RNA2.first.read',
  'Start.of.RNA2.first.read',
  'RNA2.strand')

min_ratio <- 0.7

RNA_names <- list()
for (sample.i in spt[['samplename']]){
  if (!is.null(nrow(sig.chimeras[[sample.i]])) & (nrow(sig.chimeras[[sample.i]]) > 1)) {
    RNA_names[[sample.i]] <- cbind(
      RNA1_name=rep("", nrow(sig.chimeras[[sample.i]])),
      RNA2_name=rep("", nrow(sig.chimeras[[sample.i]]))
    )

    # Prepare GRanges ahead of time
    fragment.chimera.df <- fragments[[sample.i]] %>% filter(type == 'chimera') # all chimeras, significant or not
    fragment.gr.1 <- convert_to_Granges(fragment.chimera.df[RNA1_cols_fg]) # all hits (chimera or not) for RNA1, as GRanges
    fragment.gr.2 <- convert_to_Granges(fragment.chimera.df[RNA2_cols_fg]) # all hits (chimera or not) for RNA2, as GRanges

    # For each chimera, get all associated reads 
    for(chi.i in 1:nrow(sig.chimeras[[sample.i]])) {

      # Split significant chimera into RNA1 portion and RNA2 portions; gather
      # all overlapping hits from full (significant or not) fragments; our
      # target fragments are those that overlap in both RNA1 and RNA2.
      target_chimera.1 <- convert_to_Granges(sig.chimeras[[sample.i]][chi.i, RNA1_cols])
      target_chimera.2 <- convert_to_Granges(sig.chimeras[[sample.i]][chi.i, RNA2_cols])
      hits.1 <- as.matrix(findOverlaps(fragment.gr.1, target_chimera.1))
      hits.2 <- as.matrix(findOverlaps(fragment.gr.2, target_chimera.2))
      hits.all <- data.table(rbind(hits.1, hits.2), key="queryHits,subjectHits")
      hits.both <- unique(hits.all[duplicated(hits.all)])
      target_fragments <- fragment.chimera.df[as.numeric(hits.both$queryHits),]

      # for those reads, get the names of the genes associated to RNA1
      RNA1_gr <- fragment.gr.1[as.numeric(hits.both$queryHits),]
      RNA1_names <- findGeneNamesByOverlaps(RNA1_gr, annotation, min_ratio)

      # and to RNA2
      RNA2_gr <- fragment.gr.2[as.numeric(hits.both$queryHits),]
      RNA2_names <- findGeneNamesByOverlaps(RNA2_gr, annotation, min_ratio)

      # append to larger RNA_names list
      RNA_names[[sample.i]][chi.i,] <- c(RNA1_names, RNA2_names)
    }
  }
}
```

```{r get_other_meta, results='asis', cache=TRUE, dependson='get_RNAnames', eval=FALSE}
unified_fns <- list()
```

```{r sig.summary}
    df.i[['RNA1_name']] <- get_ann_col(df.i[['RNA1.EcoCyc.ID']], 'gene_name')
    df.i[['RNA2_name']] <- get_ann_col(df.i[['RNA2.EcoCyc.ID']], 'gene_name')
    df.i[['RNA1_description']] <- get_ann_col(df.i[['RNA1.EcoCyc.ID']], 'gene_function')
    df.i[['RNA2_description']] <- get_ann_col(df.i[['RNA2.EcoCyc.ID']], 'gene_function')

}


# merge inner the replicates
common_cols <- c('TypeRNA1', 'TypeRNA2', 'RNA1_name', 'RNA2_name',
  'RNA1_description', 'RNA2_description', 'RNA1.strand', 'RNA2.strand')
for (gp in names(unified_fns)) {
  if (all(common_cols %in% names(sig.chimeras[[ unified_fns[[gp]][[1]] ]])) &
      all(common_cols %in% names(sig.chimeras[[ unified_fns[[gp]][[2]] ]]))) {

    sig.chimeras[[gp]] <- merge(sig.chimeras[[ unified_fns[[gp]][[1]] ]],
                              sig.chimeras[[ unified_fns[[gp]][[2]] ]],
                              by=common_cols,
                              suffixes=c('.1', '.2'))

  } else {

    sig.chimeras[[gp]] <- data.frame(
      matrix(ncol=length(common_target_cols),nrow=0, dimnames=list(NULL, common_target_cols))
      )
  }
}

# save the results in excel file
exported_excel(sig.chimeras, unified_fns,
               file=paste0('Summary_RILSeq_S-chimeras_', subgroup_i, '.xlsx'))
```

# Summary_interactions_with_IP

```{r, results='asis'}
cat(paste0('\n\n**Link to output file:** [Summary_interactions_with_IP_',
           subgroup_i, '.xlsx](Summary_interactions_with_IP_', subgroup_i, '.xlsx).'))
```

The RILseq output files `{sample}_all_fragments.txt`, containing all single and chimera fragments, and
the BAM files containing all mapped reads, are used to
generate the `Summary_interactions_with_IP.xlsx` file.

Briefly, the read IDs corresponding to either chimera reads or single reads were extracted from
the files `{sample}_all_fragments.txt`. BAM files were then subsetted by those read IDs to
generate BAM files of chimera reads only or of single reads only. `feat**ureCounts` was used with the
following parameters to count the reads mapping to any features from the updated annotation:

- `-t 3UTR,IGR,5UTR,AS,exon,IGT,mRNA,other-ncRNA,cis_AS_with_trans_t`: include all features
- `-g gene_name `: specify attribute type in GTF annotation to use as name
- `-s 2`: reverse stranded library
- `-O`: assign reads to all their overlapping features
- `-M`: multi-mapping reads will also be counted
- `--primary`: count primary alignments only
- `--ignoreDup`: ignore duplicate reads in read counting. The whole read pair is ignored if one of the reads is a duplicate read for paired end data.
- `-p`: specify that input data contain paired-end reads
- `-P`: check validity of paired-end distance when counting read pairs. Use -d and -D to set thresholds
- `-B`: only count read pairs that have both ends aligned.

BAM files from the Total RNAseq with matching samples, experiment `rnaseq-FMD-20190507`, were
processed the same way.

The output excel file contains tabs with the following information:

- `RILseq_all_chimeras` and `RILseq_singles` include the raw RILseq count per feature and sample. FPM means
  fragment per million, the raw count per feature was multiplied by 1e6 and divided by total in either chimera
  or single read subset.

- `totalRNA` tab contains the raw and FPM counts from the total RNA-seq 20190507.

- `IP_only` tab summarizes the IP enrichment calculations.

  The concept of IP enrichment is comparing the RNA fraction bound by Hfq (Hfq IP) to the total RNA level (total RNA-seq 20190507).
  The RIL-Seq, single + chimeras, give us the information of Hfq IP RNA:

  IP enrichment = Hfq IP / Total RNA = (RILseq_chimeras + RILseq_singles) / Total RNA

  All the numbers are FPM. The normalization is recalculated on the total RILseq_chimeras + RILseq_singles, see the
  sample-specific tabs:

- Sample-specific tabs contain the same raw counts and FPM as `RILseq_all_chimeras`, `RILseq_singles` and
  `totalRNA`, grouped per sample type and for replicate 1 (R1) and replciate 2 (R2). It also contains all the
  calculations for the `IP_only` tab, generated as follow:

  - Counts Total RILseq is the average of raw counts chimera and singles, for each replicate.

  - FPM Total RILseq is Counts Total RILseq normalized to total reads in chimera and single

  - IP enrich R1 = FPM Total RILseq R1 / FPM totalRNA R1 ; same calculation for R2

  - IP enrich average is the IP enrich R1 and IP enrich R2



```{r read_rawcounts}
get_rawfn <- function(group) {
  return(paste0('../data/rnaseq_rilseq/featurecounts_', group, '.txt'))
  }

raw.counts <- list()

cleanup <- list('chimera' = '_chimera.bam',
                'single' = '_single.bam',
                'bulkRNAseq' = '.cutadapt.markdups.bam')

ann_df <- ann_df %>%
  distinct(gene_name, .keep_all = TRUE)

for (sbst in c('chimera', 'single', 'bulkRNAseq')) {
  raw.counts[[sbst]] <- read.csv(get_rawfn(sbst), sep='\t', comment.char='#', check.names=FALSE)
  # clean up column names
  names(raw.counts[[sbst]]) <- lapply(names(raw.counts[[sbst]]), function(x) {
    gsub("^.*/", "", x)}) %>% unlist()
  names(raw.counts[[sbst]]) <- lapply(names(raw.counts[[sbst]]), function(x) {
    gsub(cleanup[[sbst]], "", x)}) %>% unlist()
  # add gene type
  raw.counts[[sbst]][['Type']] <- lapply(raw.counts[[sbst]][['Geneid']], function(x) {
    ann_df[ ann_df[['gene_name']] == x, 'type.1'] })
}
```

```{r calc_norm}
# sample names do not match between RILseq and RNAseq,
# using named list to match the samplenames
sample_match <- function(x) {
  # cover all corner-cases of samplenames
  stringr::str_replace(x, '-antiHfq', '_totalRNA_noIP') %>%
    stringr::str_replace('antiHfq', 'totalRNA_noIP') %>%
    stringr::str_replace('antiFLAG', 'totalRNA_noIP') %>%
    stringr::str_replace('ctrlplasmid_IP', 'ctrlplasmid_totalRNA') %>%
    stringr::str_replace('t4rnl1_IP', 't4rnl1_totalRNA') %>%
    stringr::str_replace('_input', '')
}

#  list('R16A_antiHfq_1'=' R16A_totalRNA_noIP_1',

for (sbst in c('chimera', 'single', 'bulkRNAseq')) {
  for (sp in spt[['samplename']] ) {
    if (sbst == 'bulkRNAseq') {
      spname <- sample_match(sp)
    } else {
      spname <- sp
    }
    total <- raw.counts[[sbst]][[spname]] %>% sum()
    raw.counts[[sbst]][[paste0('FPM_', spname)]] <- raw.counts[[sbst]][[spname]] * 1e6 / total
  }
}
```

```{r sample_spe_tabs}
sp.tabs <- list()

# set the order of columns in final table
  # Gene ID
  # Counts RILseq chimeras R1
  # Counts RILseq singles R1
  # Counts total RNA singles R1
  # Counts Total RILseq R1
  # FPM RILseq chimeras R1
  # FPM RILseq Singles R1
  # FPM Total RILseq R1
  # FPM total RNA singles R1
  # IP enrich R1
  # same for R2
  # IP enrich av WT
col_idx_order <- c(1, 2, 6, 10, 14, 4, 8, 15, 12, 18,
                      3, 7, 11, 15, 5, 9, 17, 13, 19,
                      20)

for (sp in unique(spt[['group']])) {
  cols <- c('Geneid', paste0(sp, '_1'), paste0(sp, '_2'),
             paste0('FPM_', sp, '_1'), paste0('FPM_', sp, '_2'))
  bulkRNAcols <- c('Geneid', paste0(sample_match(sp), '_1'), paste0(sample_match(sp), '_2'),
             paste0('FPM_', sample_match(sp), '_1'), paste0('FPM_', sample_match(sp), '_2'))

  # merge the chimera, single and bulk total RNA, using the Geneid as index
  sp.tabs[[sp]] <- merge(raw.counts[['chimera']][cols], raw.counts[['single']][cols],
                         by='Geneid', suffixes=c('_chimera', '_single'))
  if (all(cols %in% names(raw.counts[['bulkRNAseq']])) ) {
    sp.tabs[[sp]] <- merge(sp.tabs[[sp]],
                         raw.counts[['bulkRNAseq']][bulkRNAcols],
                         by='Geneid', suffixes=c('', '_totalRNA'))
  }
  # add total RILseq (chimera + single)) and recalculate FPM
  sp.tabs[[sp]][['Counts Total RILseq R1']] <- sp.tabs[[sp]][[paste0(sp, '_1_chimera')]] +
                                               sp.tabs[[sp]][[paste0(sp, '_1_single')]]
  sp.tabs[[sp]][['FPM Total RILseq R1']] <- sp.tabs[[sp]][['Counts Total RILseq R1']] * 1e6 /
                                               sum(sp.tabs[[sp]][['Counts Total RILseq R1']] )
  sp.tabs[[sp]][['Counts Total RILseq R2']] <- sp.tabs[[sp]][[paste0(sp, '_2_chimera')]] +
                                               sp.tabs[[sp]][[paste0(sp, '_2_single')]]
  sp.tabs[[sp]][['FPM Total RILseq R2']] <- sp.tabs[[sp]][['Counts Total RILseq R2']] * 1e6 /
                                               sum(sp.tabs[[sp]][['Counts Total RILseq R2']] )
  # calculate IP and average replicates
  if (all(cols %in% names(raw.counts[['bulkRNAseq']])) ) {
    sp.tabs[[sp]][['IP enrich R1']] <- sp.tabs[[sp]][['FPM Total RILseq R1']] /
                                     sp.tabs[[sp]][[paste0('FPM_', sample_match(sp), '_1')]]
    sp.tabs[[sp]][['IP enrich R2']] <- sp.tabs[[sp]][['FPM Total RILseq R2']] /
                                     sp.tabs[[sp]][[paste0('FPM_', sample_match(sp), '_2')]]
    sp.tabs[[sp]][['IP enrich average']] <- (sp.tabs[[sp]][['IP enrich R1']] + sp.tabs[[sp]][['IP enrich R2']])/2
    # reorganize columns according to template file
    sp.tabs[[sp]] <- sp.tabs[[sp]][col_idx_order]
  }
}
```

```{r IP_tab}
# Gene.ID	IP.enrich.av.WT	IP.enrich.av.D9A	IP.enrich.av.R16A	IP.enrich.av.Y25D	IP.enrich.av.K31A
ip.tab <- sp.tabs[[1]]['Geneid']
for (sp in unique(spt[['group']])) {
  if ('IP enrich average' %in% names(sp.tabs[[sp]] )) {
    ip.tab <- merge(ip.tab,
                  sp.tabs[[sp]][c('Geneid', 'IP enrich average')] %>% 
                    rename_with(~paste0(., '_', sp), -Geneid),
                  by='Geneid')
  }
}
```

```{r excel2}
tabs.names <- list('chimera' = 'RILseq_all_chimeras',
                   'single' = 'RILseq_singles',
                   'bulkRNAseq' = 'Total_RNAseq')

# save the results in excel file
exported_excel2 <- function(raw.counts, sp.tabs, ip.tab, file='Summary_interactions_with_IP.xlsx'){
  wb <- openxlsx::createWorkbook()

  # add the raw and normalized counts
  for (gp in names(raw.counts)) {
    openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb, tabs.names[[gp]])
    openxlsx::writeData(wb, tabs.names[[gp]], x=raw.counts[[gp]], withFilter=FALSE)
  }

  # add the IP results
  openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb, 'IP_only')
  openxlsx::writeData(wb, 'IP_only', x=ip.tab, withFilter=FALSE)

  # add individual sample group tabs
  for (sp in names(sp.tabs)) {
    openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb, sp)
    openxlsx::writeData(wb, sp, x=sp.tabs[[sp]], withFilter=FALSE)
  }

  openxlsx::saveWorkbook(wb, file=file, overwrite=TRUE)
}

exported_excel2(raw.counts, sp.tabs, ip.tab,
                file=paste0('Summary_interactions_with_IP_', subgroup_i, '.xlsx'))
```
